messages:
Sam (Sales): Heads up — Equinox legal signed off on the term sheet but they need a concrete capacity plan (throughput, reserved GPUs, autoscale behavior, preheat). Need a customer-facing plan by Monday.
Rina (Solutions Eng): Ok. quick clarifying Qs: p95/p99 latency targets? steady vs peak RPS?
Sam (Sales): They want p99 < 300ms for short chat completions. Traffic: steady 350 qps daytime, peaks to ~1200 qps during 5–15min promo bursts a few times/day. Also heavy nightly batch embeddings (2k reqs/min).
Devon (Platform): For sizing we’ll split chat vs embeddings workloads. embeddings are batch-friendly — need reserved GPUs for throughput. Chat needs low-latency small-GPU pool. Any AZ/DR constraints?
Sam (Sales): Yes — cross-AZ redundancy required. They prefer Dedicated in us-east-1 with hosted fallback in other regions.
Anika (Infra): Recommendation: mirror pools across two AZs. Example: pool-east-1a + pool-east-1b, each with reserved GPUs so failover is fast.
Rina (Solutions Eng): I ran a short perf job on their sample payloads (job=eqx-1747):
```
model: rdx-embed-1.0-q4_0
emb/s per GPU (opt): 3800
p95 latency: ~90ms
recommended steady pool for embeddings: 4 GPUs (handles 24000 emb/s theoretical, comfortable for nightly jobs)
burst suggestion: +2 GPUs for promo spikes
```
Rina (Solutions Eng): Chat model rdx-chat-small-q4: one GPU sustains ~700 short-chat qps with p95 ~220ms. So two GPUs active covers steady + buffer.
Anika (Infra): Cross-AZ topology idea: provision 3 reserved GPUs per AZ (total 6 reserved), keep min active 3 (one per AZ + one spare), scale within reserved to 6, allow burst to 8 using reserved burst credits. Configure routing to keep sessions sticky per AZ until failure.
Devon (Platform): Autoscale policy draft: min_reserved_gpus: 3, max_reserved_gpus: 6, max_burst_gpus: 8; scale_up when queue_depth > 200 for >90s; scale_down cooldown 300s. Will provide YAML snippet for SOW.
Sam (Sales): Pricing: Equinox expects an enterprise discount on monthly reserved costs. They want a blended monthly number (reserved base) + usage for burst. Is that standard?
Devon (Platform): Yes — base monthly fee for reserved 6 GPUs, burst billed as usage. I'll run pricing calc once Sam confirms target discount band.
Rina (Solutions Eng): Operational notes: recommend KV-cache warmup for top 10k prefixes and cron preheat 15 minutes before known promo windows. Warmup script example:
```
for p in $(cat hot-prefixes.txt); do
  curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"model":"rdx-chat-small-q4","input":"'$p'"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate >/dev/null
done
```
Rina (Solutions Eng): Warmup reduces cold p95 by ~35% in our test cluster.
Anika (Infra): Failover policy: if local AZ capacity exhausted, route to sibling AZ; if total reserved exhausted, route to hosted pool with a throttling policy and alert to ops. Also enable per-request audit logs and KMS — Equinox insisted on that.
Sam (Sales): They also asked for SLA language for Dedicated pools (99.9% uptime) — can we commit?
Devon (Platform): We can offer SLA for Dedicated with scheduled maintenance windows in the SOW. I'll draft the SLA clause and include MTTR/MTTA expectations.
capacity-bot: action created: eqx-capacity-plan (owner: Rina). due: 48h.
Rina (Solutions Eng): Next steps: I’ll assemble a 1-page summary (pool counts, autoscale config YAML, preheat schedule, failover notes, perf numbers) and drop into this thread by tomorrow AM. Anika will add AZ diagram, Devon will provide pricing table and SLA snippet.
Sam (Sales): Perfect. I’ll confirm the discount tier with the buyer and share their approved SKU targets by EOD. Monday 10am sync to finalize. :thumbsup:
